title: Leaving the Venue
text: “Well, I figured it didn’t matter much either way, so sure. Actually, if Motoyasu-kun’s story is anything to go by, this is where the real show begins. Sorry about this, Theo.”
“No, no, I have no idea what’s coming, but I’ll follow you wherever this goes.”
“Right. That said… Wolf, I know you want to come, but I can’t exactly bring you into the castle, so bear with it, okay?”
“Vau vau! Awoooo!”

Father spent a good while soothing Wolf, who was throwing an absolute fit about being left behind. In the end, to keep Wolf occupied until we reached the castle, Father resorted to throwing a stick and having Wolf fetch it, over and over.
“Alright! Filolial-sama! Let us devour every last morsel of the extravagant feast the castle has to offer, indeed!”
Let’s clean out the castle’s storerooms, shall we.
“Waaah!”
Just then, some of the folks from Lute Village called out to us.
“Um, excuse me…”
“Hm? Something you need from us?”
Ah, this was just like our time back in Melromarc, indeed—Father answered them with his usual easygoing warmth.
“Thank you so much. If it weren’t for all of you, I think everyone here would’ve been in real danger.”
“O-oh, you’re welcome. No injuries, I hope?”
“We’re fine. No casualties at all… and the village came through safely too.”
“Th-that’s good to hear. I imagine rebuilding will be tough, but hang in there, alright?”
“Yes, thank you so much! Um, actually…”

The villager glanced at the mongrel lizardman and the rabbit man before turning back to Father. Ah, right—those two were the notorious “abuse duo” of the circus, apparently well-remembered by everyone.
“Next time you come, we’ll make sure to arrange a proper venue for the circus.”
“Sure thing. Appreciate it. Since you’ll be dealing with rebuilding costs, we’ll keep the price low.”
“Actually… we were rather hoping for a performance that isn’t, um, tailored to this particular country’s tastes.”

Oh? So they wanted a show that wasn’t born purely out of gratitude-fueled abuse. Frankly, even I had my doubts about subjecting the heroes of the wave to an abuse show as some sort of celebration. The villagers bowed deeply and made their way back to their homes. The whole scene practically radiated relief.
“Well then, let’s head off.”

And so, we made our way to the castle to attend the feast being held there. Along the way, Father grumbled about how, once the banquet was over, he’d have to cook a mountain of food for everyone anyway—and that would probably be more exhausting than the feast itself. Apparently Panda’s foster father was already handling the prep work in advance.
“It’d be a huge help if all the Filolials eat a ton at the castle.”
“Everyone, give it your all, I say!”
“Waaah!”
Heh heh… the Crimson Swine and Trash are about to face my ultimate harassment strategy—one that doubles as a plan to satisfy Filolial-sama’s bottomless stomach.
“Ohh, magnificent! Truly the heroes’ doing! The damage this time compared to before—night and day, I tell you! I simply cannot hide my astonishment!”

The sun had set, and the banquet was underway. Trash was rattling off the same tired lines he always did, seemingly never getting bored of them. Hm? Somewhere in my memories, Father and Itsuki are pointing out that of course it’s the same—it’s a loop, after all. Must be my imagination. Itsuki, you really are insufferable this time around. Now, how shall I deal with you this loop? I was asked to try all sorts of things before introducing Fleon-chan to him, but nothing’s quite clicking yet. Is there no way to make Itsuki suffer some clear, unmistakable consequence—something severe enough to actually make him reconsider his ways? After all, Father can beat him black and blue and the man’s nerves still won’t break.
“Ohh, this has quite the flavor. Such a shame Wolf and the others can’t partake. Honestly, it’s hard to imagine someone like me even being allowed at an event like this.”
The rabbit man spoke up to Father, practically buzzing with excitement as he ate at the castle banquet.
“Funny, for someone who talks himself down so much, you’ve actually got decent table manners, Theo.”
“That part doesn’t quite click for me either, honestly. I feel like I must’ve learned it as a child, but…”
The mongrel lizardman seemed to have no trouble with table manners either. Incidentally, Big Sister apparently picked hers up later—she can even use chopsticks now, I hear.
“Dig in! Seconds, please!”
Everyone was happily helping themselves to the buffet-style spread, each in their own way.
“Huh? Already out? More, pleeease.”
Food kept getting replenished, but Filolial-sama and company were demolishing it the instant it arrived.
“Waah, Shadow Saint, if you don’t eat while you can, the darkness’ll get the jump on you when it comes!”
“Ugh…”
Ren, still looking queasy, was lying across some chairs set up in the corner, with Kuro-chan pestering him relentlessly.
“Ren-sama’s condition has worsened because of you.”
“Get back to your master.”
“Ehh…”

One of Ren’s companions gently scolded Kuro, urging her to return to our side, but Kuro-chan paid it no mind whatsoever. Somehow this brought back memories of another loop—one where Ren reunited with Fleon-chan, and Black Thunder and Ren’s companions all fought together as part of the Sacred Bird Knight Order in the end.
“Everyone’s really eating a lot, huh.”
“It’s quite the feast. I’m looking forward to trying Iwatani-sama’s cooking too. If he can recreate it as closely as possible, I’m sure everyone would be delighted.”
“You’re quietly a bit of a glutton too, Theo. Maybe eat a little more calmly, like Shion does?”
“Ha, that’s asking the impossible. I’m worn out today. Speaking of which… where did Shion go?”

The mongrel lizardman had apparently gone to fill a plate but hadn’t come back. Wandering off somewhere, was he? Itsuki might come sauntering over any moment now, wearing that righteous face of his. Well, the whole slave business was already settled back at the Dragon Hourglass, so if the Crimson Swine or Trash want to stir up trouble, it’ll have to be over something else.
“…Something feels off. Let’s slip away in the confusion and go find Shion too.”
“I really wish he’d just leave a proper message.”
“Shion tends to carry a lot on his own shoulders. I wish he’d rely on us a bit more.”
Father opened up the slave crest to check where the mongrel lizardman was.
“This way.”
“Shall we head off, then?”
Part of me wanted to keep watching the feast fill Filolial-sama’s belly forever, but since Father and the others were heading out, I decided to tag along.
“Yuki-chan, keep an eye on everyone for me, indeed! Eat to your heart’s content!”
“Leave it to me! Kuro, you eat more too!”
“Yeah! Hey, Shadow Saint, what’s this drink?”
“Ugh…”

Ren was still sprawled across the row of chairs. How long does he plan on lying there? Better answer Kuro-chan’s request and eat something, I say. With such thoughts drifting through my mind, we quietly slipped out of the party hall at a brisk pace, moved into the garden, and followed wherever Father led. Before long… we found ourselves on the path leading down to the underground dungeon. Where in the world was the mongrel lizardman headed? Just as I wondered that, a figure came into view up ahead—walking with surprising confidence.
“You’d think there’d be guards posted here, but there aren’t any.”
“Now that you mention it, yeah… Shion seems to be moving carefully too, like he’s on guard for something…”

Indeed, not a soul in sight. No doubt the Melromarc soldiers had abandoned their posts just so they could watch some scheme to humiliate Father unfold. That’s exactly the sort of thing they’d pull. And while they were busy plotting whatever this was, Father and I slipped out of the venue and were now wandering around like this. Since we’d left the lively party hall so quietly, the watchers keeping tabs on us had grown rather lax. Incidentally, if there’s ever something questionable enough that we need to move unseen, I can simply use Cloaking Lance or a concealment spell to hide us—letting us stroll about as boldly as we please.
“Still… who’d have thought he’d pull something like this.”
“In the loop you remember, Motoyasu-kun, Shion wasn’t the type to do this kind of thing?”
“Indeed not.”

In the loop where the mongrel lizardman had been Father’s very first slave, what he did after the wave ended, back at the party hall, was simply eat quietly beside Father, much like Big Sister did. This wandering off was quite unexpected, by contrast.
“Well, maybe he figures it’s fine to slip away since Motoyasu-kun, Theo, and all the Filolials are here?”
And so, where the mongrel lizardman was headed was…
